title: Iran Football Federation President Mehdi Taj Denied Entry to Canada at Toronto Airport — Misses FIFA Congress
detail: Iran Football Federation President Mehdi Taj, Secretary-General Hedayat Mombeni, and Deputy Secretary-General Hamed Momeni arrived at Toronto Pearson International Airport with valid visas on April 29–30 but were refused entry to Canada and returned to Turkey on the first available flight. Canadian authorities cited Canada's 2024 designation of Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) as a terrorist organization, stating that Taj held ties to IRGC-linked institutions that rendered him inadmissible under Canadian law. Canadian Foreign Affairs Minister Anita Anand acknowledged the denial while calling it 'unintentional' — a characterization rejected by the Iranian delegation, which described the treatment as an 'insult.' The three officials missed the 76th FIFA Congress entirely. AFC General Secretary Windsor John had said as recently as April 29 that he was 'optimistic' Iran's delegation would arrive in time for the Congress. FIFA President Infantino said he would arrange a meeting with the delegation at FIFA headquarters in Zurich. The denial dramatically escalated the Iranian participation crisis: if federation leadership cannot enter Canada to attend an administrative congress 42 days before the tournament, the ability of 26 players, coaches, medical personnel, and official delegates to obtain US and Canadian visas and travel safely to Group G matches in Los Angeles (June 15 vs. New Zealand, June 21 vs. Belgium) and Seattle (June 26 vs. Egypt) is deeply in question. Iran International reported that Taj's IRGC connections were the specific legal basis for the Canadian border agency's refusal.

media.caption: Iran's football federation president Mehdi Taj and two senior officials denied entry to Canada at Toronto Pearson Airport due to IRGC designation — miss FIFA Congress entirely, return to Turkey

title: Iran Sports Minister: Nation 'Under No Circumstances' Can Participate in 2026 World Cup — Warm-Up Friendlies Cancelled
detail: Iran Minister of Sport and Youth Ahmad Donyamali issued his most definitive statement yet on April 30, declaring that Iran 'under no circumstances' can participate in the 2026 World Cup — going beyond his April 21 'maybe the decision is not to go' language and directly contradicting the April 23 statement by government spokesperson Ali Mohajerani that Iran was 'fully prepared for effective participation.' The statement was issued hours after Iranian football federation officials were denied entry to Canada at Toronto Pearson Airport and missed the FIFA Congress. Separately, Iran's pre-tournament warm-up friendlies — scheduled to take place in the weeks before the June 11 tournament opening — were cancelled without explanation, removing a key mechanism for the squad to maintain fitness and team cohesion before the tournament. FourFourTwo confirmed the cancellations. The combination of federation leadership denied entry to the FIFA Congress, the Sports Minister's unequivocal language, and the cancelled friendlies represented the most severe convergence of signals yet that Iran will formally withdraw before the June 1 squad submission deadline. Iran would be the first country to withdraw from a World Cup after qualifying since 1950. No replacement team has been publicly identified by FIFA, though Iraq and the UAE were cited as the most likely AFC candidates.

media.caption: Iran Sports Minister Ahmad Donyamali says Iran 'under no circumstances' can participate in the 2026 World Cup — issued hours after federation officials were denied entry to Canada

title: 76th FIFA Congress Opens in Vancouver With Iran Absent — First FIFA Congress in Canada Since Montreal 1976
detail: The 76th FIFA Congress opened at the Vancouver Convention Centre on April 30, bringing together representatives of all 211 FIFA member associations 42 days before the June 11 tournament opening. More than 1,600 delegates attended, generating an estimated CAD $4.9 million in local economic impact. The Congress — the first held in Canada since Montreal in 1976 — served as the formal gathering ahead of the tournament, addressing governance, competition format, and fiscal matters. The conspicuous absence of Iran's football federation delegation — denied entry at Toronto Pearson Airport hours earlier — dominated media attention and overshadowed other business. The agenda also included the 2027 FIFA Women's World Cup bid process (USA and CONCACAF submitted a joint bid for 2031; England, Ireland, Scotland, and Wales confirmed a joint bid for 2035), and FIFA presidential re-election procedures for the 2027–2031 term. CTV News and CBC Sports reported strong Canadian public interest in the Congress as a preview of Canada's expanded role in co-hosting the tournament — Canadian cities Toronto, Vancouver, and Edmonton will collectively host 13 matches.

media.caption: 76th FIFA Congress opens at the Vancouver Convention Centre on April 30 — Iran absent after officials denied entry; first FIFA Congress in Canada since Montreal 1976

title: CAF Unanimously Backs Infantino's Re-election as FIFA President for 2027–2031 Term
detail: The Confederation of African Football (CAF), representing all 54 African member associations, announced unanimous support for FIFA President Gianni Infantino's re-election to a further four-year term (2027–2031) at the Vancouver Congress. The endorsement, reported by Daily Sports and confirmed by multiple FIFA Congress reporters, solidifies Infantino's hold on the FIFA presidency ahead of the formal election process. CAF's 54 votes represent the largest bloc in FIFA's 211-member structure. The endorsement came at a moment of heightened scrutiny for Infantino — Vancouver Police had denied his request for a presidential-level motorcade escort the previous day, and the Iranian federation crisis was generating significant negative press for FIFA's handling of the World Cup political fallout. Infantino's first term as FIFA president began in 2016; he was re-elected in 2019 and again in 2023 and is the architect of the expanded 48-team World Cup format.

media.caption: CAF's 54 member associations unanimously back Infantino's re-election as FIFA president for a 2027–2031 term at the Vancouver Congress

title: NPR: Soccer Fans Globally Sitting Out 2026 World Cup Over Ticket Prices and US Immigration Enforcement
detail: NPR published a major report on April 30 documenting why international soccer fans are opting out of attending the 2026 World Cup in the United States despite the tournament's historic scale. The report cited three converging deterrents: (1) ticket prices — with average resale prices far exceeding the Qatar 2022 tournament and the cheapest group-stage tickets on secondary markets approaching four figures — creating affordability barriers even for fans from wealthy nations; (2) US immigration enforcement — with 39 countries under travel restrictions and widespread anxiety among fans from Latin America, the Middle East, and Africa about ICE operations near tournament venues; and (3) hotel market instability — with host cities reporting lower-than-expected hotel bookings and FIFA having cancelled large blocks of hotel room reservations in some host cities. The report quoted individual fans from Mexico, Brazil, and Nigeria who had intended to attend but decided against it. Sky Sports' live World Cup update blog also noted the attendance concern was a consistent topic at the Vancouver Congress. The NPR report added quantitative texture to what HRW, Amnesty International, and the ACLU had warned about in their spring 2026 reports — that the combination of US immigration policy and FIFA's pricing model risked stripping the tournament of its authentic supporter atmosphere.

media.caption: NPR documents global soccer fans opting out of 2026 World Cup over unaffordable tickets, US immigration enforcement anxiety, and hotel market uncertainty
